This is a proposed CPU qualification contract, not an executable runner or authorization. Freeze the completed source, artifacts, runner, corpus and criteria before any baseline or candidate execution. A missing reference or undefined expected value is a blocked criterion, never an automatic pass.

Use a fresh standard Windows account or VM with a verified distinct SID, no ordinary library/connectors/credentials, and an isolated data root. Runtime network must be denied outside the Python process as well as observed inside it. No resident Uoink helper or port 5179 access is permitted. Fix the target CPython 3.13 interpreter, Windows AMD64 wheels and local DLL search paths by hash. Disable PyAnnote metrics before imports. Run one model process at a time; retain actual child and outer exits, stdout/stderr, loaded module/DLL identities, resource measurements and all refusals. Instrumentation changes require their own brief and preserved failed attempts.

Proposed order and measurable gates:

| Stage | Inputs and operation | Required recorded result |

The corpus itself is not yet produced or approved. A concrete proposed minimum is ten hashed 16-kHz mono WAV files: ten-second silence; a ten-second non-speech tone; six short clean spoken utterances with manually recorded word and utterance boundaries; one long utterance crossing the five-second VAD window; and one clip containing two utterances separated by a known silence. Spoken text must include ordinary prose, a proper name, a date, an amount and a negation. This specifies coverage, not nonexistent audio bytes or fabricated annotations. Freeze the exact text, waveform hashes, speakers' permission and annotations before testing. No TTS/model provider, audio fetch or use of private library audio is authorized here.

Proposed quality criteria for owner review are: zero segments for silence; the non-speech tone's expected outcome fixed by manual annotation before execution; no hallucinated words on either nonspeech fixture; corpus word-error rate at most 5% on the short clean-speech set; exact proper name/date/amount/negation tokens; median absolute utterance-boundary error at most 250 ms and maximum at most 750 ms. All timestamps must lie within [0,duration], with start <= end. Fix normalization rules before scoring and retain raw text. These are proposed acceptance thresholds, not measured capabilities.

For a before/after claim, use a separately approved, safe baseline producing the same metrics on the same frozen corpus and hardware. Existing product/unit/navigation receipts cannot substitute for an ASR numerical baseline. Do not run the unsafe historical pickle loader to obtain an oracle. Candidate word-error rate may increase by at most one absolute percentage point versus that approved baseline, median boundary error by at most 100 ms, and median wall time/peak private memory by at most 25%. Apply the absolute criteria too. If no safe baseline exists, report the absolute results and leave numerical/performance non-regression unproved; Ryan must decide whether that evidence is sufficient before release.

Use proposed trial ceilings of 6 GiB process memory and 600 seconds per clip for base, 12 GiB and 1,200 seconds for the remaining choices, with one process at a time and <=60-second clips. A host without sufficient headroom must not start that trial. These generous resource caps bound the experiment; they are not acceptable product latency claims. The final runner must implement and synthetically verify its external timeout/resource observation before Q2. Freeze CPU thread count, compute_type and repetition count; use three runs for median timing after a separately recorded first-load measurement. Do not silently choose GPU execution. Record every failed, refused, timed-out or incomplete attempt, then write a repair brief before any fresh-label rerun.
